page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 7.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of approximately 0.9 GB per vCPU. This configuration does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates that the n1-highcpu-8 delivers modest processing capabilities. Its single-core and multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng, falls within the bottom 25% of tested servers. Similarly, the Geekbench single-core score of 914.0 and multi-core score of 3557.0 are positioned in the poor and weak categories respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance for large block read and write operations, but cached small block reads remain in the bottom 25%.

Due to its low memory allocation of 7.0 GB for 8 vCPUs, this instance presents a clear tradeoff, limiting its utility for memory-intensive applications. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require multiple parallel execution threads but have minimal memory footprints. The server is suited for lightweight multi-threaded tasks, basic software compilation, and simple ray tracing workloads where average performance is acceptable, but it is less suitable for database operations or high-throughput web serving.
